title.analysis: Authentic title "The Invisible Prison: How Money Traps You Without You Even Realizing It" promises a hidden-mechanism exposé. The script delivers a systemic-critique essay (monthly payments, lifestyle inflation, an "ignorance tax", designed consumption) and openly says awareness may not help; the title matches the framing.

script.opening_words: You're not poor because you don't make enough money. You're poor because the system is designed to keep you that way. And the worst part is you probably don't even see it happening. Most people walk around thinking they're making rational financial decisions when they're actually trapped in an invisible prison that's been carefully constructed around them since childhood. The bars aren't made of steel. They're made of payments, subscriptions, lifestyle expectations, and the constant whisper that you deserve things
script.ending_words: struggle because that's how the math works out for most people. At least you'll know why. At least you won't spend your whole life wondering what you did wrong when the game was never designed for you to win in the first place. The invisible prison is still a prison even after you can see the bars. But knowing they're there is the first step to finding the gaps between
script.analysis: Full 21613 canonical characters read. A single-narrator essay with no composites: hook claiming the system keeps you poor, lifetime earnings vs savings, monthly-payment trap, lifestyle inflation with a friend anecdote, moving goalposts, the ignorance tax, combined traps, consumer-economy dependence, repeated $2M passage, compounding cost of small decisions, corporate psychology (phones, streaming, gyms, delivery apps), social pressure, complexity and analysis paralysis, life-stage crises, luck, guru incentives, boring fixes, and a pessimistic close. The stored text is truncated mid-sentence; several numbers are unsourced or internally inconsistent.
